paragraphs: We are an externally-advised Maryland corporation formed in 2013 that invests primarily in high revenue per available room ("RevPAR") luxury hotels and resorts. High RevPAR, for purposes of our investment strategy, means RevPAR of at least twice the then-current U.S. national average RevPAR for all hotels as determined by STR, LLC. Two times the U.S. national average RevPAR was approximately $200 for the year ended December 31, 2025. We have elected to be taxed as a REIT under the Code beginning in the year ended December 31, 2013. We conduct our business and own substantially all of our assets through our operating partnership, Braemar OP.

We operate in the direct hotel investment segment of the hotel lodging industry. As of March 9, 2026, we owned interests in 13 hotel properties in six states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico and St. Thomas, U.S. Virgin Islands with 3,028 total rooms. The hotel properties in our current portfolio are predominantly located in U.S. urban and resort locations with favorable growth characteristics resulting from multiple demand generators.

We are advised by Ashford Hospitality Advisors LLC ("Ashford LLC" or the "Advisor"), a subsidiary of Ashford Inc., through an advisory agreement. All of the hotel properties in our portfolio are currently asset-managed by Ashford LLC. Asset management functions include acquisition, renovation, financing and disposition of assets, operational accountability of managers, budget review, capital expenditures and property-level strategies as compared to the day-to-day management of our hotel properties, which is performed by our hotel managers. We do not have any employees. All of the advisory services that might be provided by employees are provided to us by Ashford LLC.

We do not operate any of our hotel properties directly; instead, we contractually engage hotel management companies to operate them for us under management contracts. Remington Hospitality, a subsidiary of Ashford Inc., manages five of our 13 hotel properties. Third-party management companies manage the remaining hotel properties.

Ashford Inc. also provides other products and services to us or our hotel properties through certain entities in which Ashford Inc. has an ownership interest. These products and services include, but are not limited to, design and construction services, debt placement and related services, audio visual services, real estate advisory and brokerage services, insurance policies covering general liability, workers compensation and business automobile claims, insurance claims services, hypoallergenic premium rooms, watersport activities, travel/transportation services and cash management services. See note 17 to our consolidated financial statements.

Mr. Monty J. Bennett is chairman and chief executive officer of Ashford Inc. and, together with Mr. Archie Bennett, Jr., as of December 31, 2025, holds a controlling interest in Ashford Inc. As of December 31, 2025, the Bennetts owned approximately 809,937 shares of Ashford Inc. common stock, which represented an approximate 51.9% ownership interest in Ashford Inc., and owned 18,758,600 shares of Ashford Inc. Series D Convertible Preferred Stock, which, along with all unpaid accrued and accumulated dividends thereon, was convertible (at a conversion price of $117.50 per share) into an additional approximate 4,573,359 shares of Ashford Inc. common stock, which if converted as of December 31, 2025 would have increased the Bennetts' ownership interest in Ashford Inc. to 87.8%. The 18,758,600 shares of Series D Convertible Preferred Stock owned by Mr. Monty J. Bennett and Mr. Archie Bennett, Jr. include 360,000 shares owned by trusts. Additionally, Mr. Monty J. Bennett acquired the right to direct votes, effective March 25, 2025, and as of December 31, 2025, those rights represented approximately 551,000 common shares.

As of December 31, 2025, Mr. Monty J. Bennett, chairman of our board of directors and his father, Mr. Archie Bennett, Jr., together owned approximately 2,472,808 shares of our common stock and common units (including long-term incentive plan ("LTIP") units and performance LTIP units), which represented an approximate 3.4% ownership in the Company.

Our principal business objectives are to generate attractive returns on our invested capital and long-term growth in cash flow to maximize total returns to our stockholders. To achieve our objectives, we pursue the following strategies:

Focused Investment Strategy. Our strategy is to invest in premium-branded and high-quality independent luxury hotels and resorts that are anticipated to generate RevPAR at least twice the average RevPAR for the U.S. lodging industry, as determined by STR, LLC and are located predominantly in the United States and its territories.

We intend to concentrate our investments in markets where we believe there are significant growth opportunities, taking into consideration the risk of additional supply. In determining anticipated RevPAR for a particular asset, we may take into account forecasts and other considerations, including without limitation, conversions or repositioning of assets, capital plans, brand changes and other factors which may reasonably be forecasted to raise RevPAR after stabilization. Stabilization with respect to a hotel, after the completion of an initiative such as a capital plan, conversion or change of brand name or change of the business mix or other operating characteristics, is generally expected to occur within 12 to 24 months after the completion of the related renovation, repositioning or brand change.

In connection with this investment strategy, we frequently evaluate opportunities to acquire additional hotel properties, either through direct ownership, joint ventures, partnership participation or similar arrangements. We may use cash or debt or issue common units or other securities of ours or our operating partnership, Braemar OP, or our other subsidiaries as currency for a transaction. Some or all of these acquisitions, if completed, may be material to our company, individually or in the aggregate. We may, from time to time, be party to letters of intent, term sheets and other non-binding agreements relating to potential acquisitions. We cannot assure you that we will enter into definitive acquisition agreements with respect to any potential acquisitions.

Asset Management Strategy. We rely on Ashford LLC to asset-manage the hotel properties in our portfolio, and will rely on Ashford LLC to asset-manage any hotel properties we may acquire in the future, to help maximize the operating performance, cash flow and value of each hotel. Asset management includes working with the hotel managers and holding them accountable to drive top line and bottom-line operating performances. Ashford LLC aims to achieve this goal by benchmarking each asset's performance compared to similar hotel properties within our portfolio. Ashford LLC also monitors hotel operating expenses. If expense levels are not commensurate with the property revenues, Ashford LLC works with the property manager to implement cost-cutting initiatives. Ashford LLC also evaluates and proposes strategies to improve the sales, marketing and revenue management efforts of the property manager as well as its ability to drive ancillary hotel revenues (e.g., spa, food and beverage, parking, and Internet). Further, Ashford LLC works with the brands and management companies to negotiate

favorable franchise agreement and hotel management agreement terms. Finally, Ashford LLC participates in brand advisory committee and industry advocacy association meetings to provide feedback and input on new hotel brand and industry initiatives.

Disciplined Capital Allocation Strategy. We intend to pursue a disciplined capital allocation strategy for the acquisition, operation, disposition and financing of assets in our portfolio and those that we may acquire in the future. Ashford LLC utilizes its extensive industry experience and capital markets expertise to influence the timing of capital deployment and recycling, and we may selectively sell hotel properties that are no longer consistent with our investment strategy or as to which returns appear to have been maximized. To the extent we sell hotel properties, we generally intend to redeploy the capital into investment opportunities that we believe will achieve higher returns, repay debt, or buy back our common stock or other securities.

headings: Summary Risk Factors
Risks Related to Our Business and Properties
Economic conditions in the United States and geopolitical developments could have a material adverse impact on our earnings and financial condition.
Our cash, cash equivalents and investments could be adversely affected if the financial institutions in which we hold our cash, cash equivalents and investments fail.
We may not pay dividends on our common stock or preferred stock in the future.

Our business is significantly influenced by the economies and other conditions in the specific markets in which we operate, particularly in the metropolitan areas where we have high concentrations of hotels.
Our investments are concentrated in the hotel industry, and our business would be adversely affected by an economic downturn in that sector.
We face risks related to changes in the global economic and political environment, including capital and credit markets.

We invest in the luxury segments of the lodging market, which are highly competitive and generally subject to greater volatility than most other market segments and could negatively affect our profitability.
We depend on Ashford LLC's key personnel with long-standing business relationships. The loss of Ashford LLC's key personnel could threaten our ability to operate our business successfully.
If we acquire additional hotel properties, we face significant competition for attractive investment opportunities from other well-capitalized investors.
There is no guarantee that Ashford Trust will sell us any of the properties that are subject to the right of first offer agreement.
We may be unable to successfully integrate and operate acquired properties, which may have a material adverse effect on our business and operating results.

Our joint venture investments could be adversely affected by our lack of sole decision-making authority, our reliance on a co-venturer's financial condition and disputes between us and our co-venturers.
Hotel franchise or management agreement requirements or the loss of such an agreement could adversely affect us.
Our management agreements could adversely affect our ability to sell or finance our hotel properties.
Seven of our hotels currently operate under Marriott or Hilton brands; therefore, we are subject to risks associated with concentrating our portfolio in just two brand families.
If we cannot obtain additional capital, our growth will be limited.
Some of our hotels are subject to ground leases; if we are found to be in breach of a ground lease or are unable to renew a ground lease, our business could be materially and adversely affected.

We are increasingly dependent on information technology, and cyber-attacks, security problems, artificial intelligence-related risks, or other disruption and expanding social media vehicles present new risks.
We may experience losses caused by severe weather conditions or natural disasters.
Changes in laws, regulations or policies may adversely affect our business.
We may from time to time be subject to litigation, which could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition, results of operations, cash flow and trading price of our common stock.
Risks Related to our Debt Financing
We have a significant amount of debt, and our organizational documents have no limitation on the amount of additional indebtedness that we may incur in the future.
Higher interest rates have increased our debt payments and such debt payments may remain high.
There is refinancing risk associated with our debt.
Our hedging strategies may not be successful in mitigating our risks associated with interest rates and could reduce the overall returns on an investment in our Company.
Risks Related to Conflicts of Interest
Ashford LLC was a subsidiary of Ashford Trust until its spin-off and may be able to direct attractive investment opportunities to Ashford Trust and away from us.
paragraphs: Our business is subject to a number of risks, including risks that may prevent us from achieving our business objectives or may adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, and prospects. These risks are discussed more fully below and include, but are not limited to, risks related to:
•our ability to raise sufficient capital and/or take other actions to improve our liquidity position or otherwise meet our liquidity requirements;

•actions by our lenders to accelerate loan balances and foreclose on the hotel properties that are security for our loans if we are unable to make debt service payments or satisfy our other obligations under the forbearance agreements;
•general volatility of the capital markets and the market price of our common and preferred stock;
•catastrophic events or geopolitical conditions, such as the conflict between Russia and Ukraine, the Israel-Palestine-Iran conflict and ongoing instability in Venezuela;
•availability, terms and deployment of capital;

paragraphs: On August 26, 2025, Braemar entered into an agreement with Ashford Inc. to explore a potential sale of Braemar. Pursuant to the Letter Agreement, Braemar and Ashford Inc. agreed that the termination fee payable to Ashford Inc. under the advisory agreement is $574.8 million (exclusive of accrued fees). However, Braemar and Ashford Inc. have agreed to the payment of a discounted aggregate amount of $480.0 million plus accrued fees. Ashford Inc. received a $17.0 million payment upon execution of the agreement. The $17.0 million payment will be credited against other amounts due to Ashford Inc. from Braemar if the sale of the Company does not occur before July 1, 2028. On December 22, 2025, Braemar entered into the Amendment. The Amendment was entered into in order to eliminate unintended ambiguity regarding the circumstances under which the termination fees become due and payable to Ashford Inc. and the timing of payment in order to more fully reflect the parties' original intent under the Letter Agreement and ensure consistency across potential transaction structures in how the proceeds from a Company Sale Transaction (as defined in the Letter Agreement) are applied.

On November 6, 2025, we sold The Clancy pursuant to an Agreement of Purchase and Sale, entered into effective October 6, 2025, for $115.0 million in cash, subject to customary pro-rations and adjustments. Additionally, the Company repaid approximately $64.7 million on the mortgage loan that was partially secured by the hotel property.

On February 20, 2026, our board of directors, in consultation with counsel, in compliance with Article II, Section 12 of the Company's bylaws, voted unanimously (with Mr. Ghassemieh recused) to determine that Mr. Ghassemieh was in breach of the cooperation agreement entered into on August 25, 2025 between the Company, Ashford Trust, Ashford Inc. and Mr. Ghassemieh (the "Ghassemieh Agreement"). Accordingly, pursuant to Section 4(a)(ii) of the Ghassemieh Agreement, Mr. Ghassemieh's irrevocable resignation letter executed by Mr. Ghassemieh in connection with the Ghassemieh Agreement became effective on February 20, 2026.

On March 5, 2026, Ashford Inc. and Ashford LLC agreed with Deric Eubanks, the Chief Financial Officer of Ashford Inc., and Ashford LLC that, effective March 31, 2026 (the "Termination Date"), Mr. Eubanks would terminate employment with and service to Ashford Inc., Ashford LLC and their affiliates. Mr. Eubanks is also the Chief Financial Officer of the Company and Ashford Trust and accordingly his service as Chief Financial Officer of each of the Company and Ashford Trust will also end effective as of the Termination Date. Effective on the Termination Date, Justin Coe, the Company's current Chief Accounting Officer and principal accounting officer, will serve as the principal financial officer of the Company.

paragraphs: 本公司為一間由外部機構管理的馬裏蘭州公司，於2013年成立，主要投資於高營業收入每可用客房（"RevPAR"）的豪華飯店與度假村。根據我們的投資策略，高RevPAR意味著RevPAR至少為當時美國國家平均RevPAR的兩倍，此平均RevPAR由STR, LLC所確定。兩倍的美國國家平均RevPAR在2025年12月31日財年約為200美元。本公司自2013年12月31日財年起已選擇以REIT方式課稅。我們的業務運作及擁有 substantially all 的資產皆透過我們的營運合夥企業 Braemar OP 進行。
我們從事飯店投資的直接投資分部。截至2026年3月9日，我們在六個州、華盛頓特區、波多黎各及美屬維京羣島的聖託馬斯擁有13間飯店的權益，總計3,028間客房。我們目前資產組閤中的飯店 predominantly 位於美國都市與度假勝地，這些地區因多種需求驅動因素而具有良好的成長潛力。

我們由 Ashford Hospitality Advisors LLC（"Ashford LLC" 或 "Advisor"），為 Ashford Inc. 的子公司，透過管理契約提供諮詢服務。我們資產組閤中所有的飯店目前皆由 Ashford LLC 進行資產管理。資產管理功能包括取得、翻修、融資與處分資產、管理者的運營責任、預算審查、資本支出與飯店層面的策略，與我們飯店的日常管理不同，日常管理由我們的飯店經理執行。我們沒有任何員工。所有可能由員工提供的諮詢服務皆由 Ashford LLC 提供給我們。
我們並未直接經營任何飯店；相反地，我們透過契約聘請飯店管理公司為我們經營飯店，並透過管理契約進行。Remington Hospitality，為 Ashford Inc. 的子公司，管理我們13間飯店中的五間。其他飯店則由第三方管理公司管理。
Ashford Inc. 也透過某些擁有權益的實體，為我們或我們的飯店提供其他產品與服務。這些產品與服務包括但不限於設計與建設服務、債務 placements 及相關服務、音響視覺服務、不動產諮詢與仲介服務、覆蓋一般責任、員工補償與商業汽車申報的保險政策、保險申報服務、過敏原低敏度豪華客房、水上活動、旅遊/交通服務與現金管理服務。詳見我們合併財務報表的附註17。

Monty J. Bennett 先生為 Ashford Inc. 的董事長兼首席執行官，與 Archie Bennett, Jr. 先生，截至2025年12月31日，共同持有 Ashford Inc. 的控制性權益。截至2025年12月31日，Bennetts 持有約809,937股 Ashford Inc. 普通股，代表約51.9% 的權益，並持有18,758,600股 Ashford Inc. 系列D可轉換優先股，加上所有未支付的累積與應計股息，可轉換（轉換價格為每股117.50美元）為額外約4,573,359股 Ashford Inc. 普通股，若於2025年12月31日轉換，將使Bennetts在Ashford Inc. 的權益增加至87.8%。Mr. Monty J. Bennett 和 Mr. Archie Bennett, Jr. 所持有的18,758,600股系列D可轉換優先股中，包含360,000股由信託持有。此外，Mr. Monty J. Bennett 於2025年3月25日取得投票權，截至2025年12月31日，這些投票權代表約551,000股普通股。
截至2025年12月31日，Mr. Monty J. Bennett，本公司董事會主席及其父親 Mr. Archie Bennett, Jr.，共同持有約2,472,808股本公司普通股及普通單位（包括長期激勵計劃（"LTIP"）單位及績效LTIP單位），代表約3.4% 的本公司權益。
我們的主要業務目標是產生對我們投資資本有吸引力的回報，並實現現金流的長期成長，以最大化對股東的總回報。為達成這些目標，我們執行以下策略：
聚焦投資策略。我們的策略是投資於高價位品牌及高品質的獨立豪華飯店與度假村，預期其每間客房營收（RevPAR）至少為美國旅館業平均RevPAR的兩倍，此平均RevPAR由STR, LLC所確定，且這些飯店與度假村主要位於美國及其屬地。
我們意圖將投資集中於我們認為有顯著成長機會的市場，同時考量額外供應的風險。在評估特定資產預期RevPAR時，我們可能考量預測及其他因素，包括但不限於資產轉型或重新定位、資本計畫、品牌變更及其他可合理預測在穩定後可能提高RevPAR的因素。對於飯店而言，在完成如資本計畫、轉型或品牌變更或業務組成變更或其他營運特徵變更等計畫後，穩定通常預期在相關翻新、重新定位或品牌變更完成後12至24個月內發生。

與此投資策略相關，我們經常評估取得更多飯店財產的機會，無論是透過直接擁有、合資企業、合作夥伴參與或其他類似安排。我們可能使用現金或債務，或發行本公司或我們營運合夥企業Braemar OP或我們其他子公司之普通單位或其他證券作為交易對價。若這些取得行動完成，其中一些或全部可能對本公司產生重大影響，個別或總體而言。我們有時可能參與意向書、條件書及其他非約束性協議，與潛在取得行動相關。我們無法保證我們會與任何潛在取得行動簽訂最終取得協議。

資產管理策略。我們依賴Ashford LLC對我們投資組閤中的飯店財產進行資產管理，並將依賴Ashford LLC對我們未來可能取得的任何飯店財產進行資產管理，以幫助最大化每間飯店的營運表現、現金流及價值。資產管理包括與飯店經理合作並使其負起責任，以推動營收與營運績效。Ashford LLC透過將每項資產的表現與我們投資組閤中類似飯店財產進行對比，以實現此目標。Ashford LLC同時監測飯店營運費用。若費用水平與財產營收不相稱，Ashford LLC會與財產經理合作實施節省成本的措施。Ashford LLC也會評估並提出策略，以改善財產經理的銷售、行銷與收入管理努力，以及其推動附加飯店收入（例如水療、餐飲、停車與網路）的能力。此外，Ashford LLC會與品牌與管理公司協商
有利的特許經營協議與飯店管理協議條款。最後，Ashford LLC參與品牌諮詢委員會與產業倡議協會會議，以提供對新飯店品牌與產業計畫的意見與建議。
嚴謹的資金配置策略。我們意圖對投資組閤中資產以及未來可能取得的資產的取得、營運、處分與融資採取嚴謹的資金配置策略。Ashford LLC運用其廣泛的產業經驗與資本市場專業知識，影響資金部署與再運用的時機，我們可能選擇性地出售不再符合我們投資策略或回報似乎已達極致的飯店財產。若我們出售飯店財產，我們通常意圖將資金重新運用至我們認為可實現更高回報、償還債務、或買回本公司普通股或其他證券的投資機會。

paragraphs: 於 2025 年 8 月 26 日，Braemar 與 Ashford Inc. 籤訂協議，探討 Braemar 可能的出售事宜。根據協議書，Braemar 與 Ashford Inc. 同意，根據諮詢協議，支付給 Ashford Inc. 的終止費用為 574.8 百萬美元（不含累計費用）。然而，Braemar 與 Ashford Inc. 同意支付總計 480.0 百萬美元加上累計費用的折扣金額。Ashford Inc. 在協議簽訂時收到 17.0 百萬美元付款。若公司在 2028 年 7 月 1 日前未完成出售，則該 17.0 百萬美元付款將抵銷 Braemar 對 Ashford Inc. 的其他應付款項。於 2025 年 12 月 22 日，Braemar 籤訂修正協議。該修正協議係為消除有關終止費用在何種情況下應支付給 Ashford Inc. 以及付款時間的誤解，以更完整反映雙方根據協議書的原始意圖，並確保在潛在交易結構中，公司出售交易（根據協議書定義）所得金額的應用方式具有一致性。
於 2025 年 11 月 6 日，本公司根據 2025 年 10 月 6 日簽訂的買賣協議，以現金 115.0 百萬美元出售 The Clancy，扣除慣常的按比例調整。此外，本公司償還約 64.7 百萬美元的抵押貸款，該貸款部分以酒店不動產為擔保。

於 2026 年 2 月 20 日，本公司董事會在與律師諮詢後，依照本公司章程第二條第十二款，一致通過（Ghassemieh 先生迴避）決定，Ghassemieh 先生違反於 2025 年 8 月 25 日與本公司、Ashford Trust、Ashford Inc. 及 Ghassemieh 先生簽訂的合作協議（稱為「Ghassemieh 協議」）。因此，根據 Ghassemieh 協議第 4(a)(ii) 條，Ghassemieh 先生於 Ghassemieh 協議簽訂時所簽署的不可撤銷辭職信，自 2026 年 2 月 20 日起生效。

於 2026 年 3 月 5 日，Ashford Inc. 與 Ashford LLC 與 Deric Eubanks，Ashford Inc. 的首席財務官，以及 Ashford LLC 同意，自 2026 年 3 月 31 日（稱為「終止日期」）起，Eubanks 先生將終止與 Ashford Inc.、Ashford LLC 及其附屬公司的僱用關係與服務。Eubanks 先生同時也是本公司與 Ashford Trust 的首席財務官，因此其作為本公司與 Ashford Trust 的首席財務官的服務關係亦於終止日期終止。自終止日期起，本公司現任首席會計官及主要會計官 Justin Coe 將擔任本公司之主要財務官。

headings: 風險因素總覽
與本公司業務及資產相關之風險
美國經濟狀況及國際政治發展可能對本公司獲利及財務狀況造成重大不利影響。
若存放本公司現金、現金等價物及投資之金融機構發生違約，本公司之現金、現金等價物及投資可能受到不利影響。
本公司未來可能無法就普通股或優先股發放股息。
本公司業務深受所從事市場之經濟及其他條件影響，特別是在本公司擁有高比例飯店之都會區。
本公司投資集中於飯店產業，若該產業發生經濟衰退，將對本公司業務造成不利影響。
本公司面臨全球經濟及政治環境變動相關風險，包括資本及信貸市場之變化。
本公司投資於旅館業市場的豪華分部，此等分部競爭激烈，且通常較其他市場分部具有更高的波動性，可能對本公司獲利能力產生負面影響。
本公司依賴 Ashford LLC 的關鍵人員及其長期的商業關係。若 Ashford LLC 的關鍵人員離職，可能威脅本公司成功運作業務的能力。
若本公司取得更多旅館不動產，將面臨來自其他資金充足的投資者對優質投資機會的激烈競爭。
無法保證 Ashford Trust 會將根據優先購買權協議所涉及的不動產出售給本公司。
本公司可能無法成功整合及運作所取得的不動產，此情形可能對本公司業務及營運成果產生重大不利影響。
本公司之合資投資可能因本公司缺乏單獨決策權、依賴合資夥伴之財務狀況及本公司與合資夥伴之間之爭議而受到不利影響。
旅館特許經營或管理協議之要求或喪失此等協議，可能對本公司產生不利影響。
本公司之管理協議可能影響本公司出售或融資旅館不動產之能力。
我們目前有七間飯店正在以 Marriott 或 Hilton 品牌營運；因此，我們面臨將投資組合集中於僅兩個品牌家族所衍生的風險。
若我們無法取得額外資金，將會限制我們的成長。
我們部分飯店受地面租賃條款約束；若我們被判定違反地面租賃條款，或無法續約地面租賃，將可能對我們的業務造成重大且不利的影響。
我們越來越依賴資訊科技，而網路攻擊、安全問題、與人工智慧相關的風險，或其他中斷以及擴展的社交媒體平台，可能帶來新的風險。
我們可能因嚴重天氣條件或自然災害而遭受損失。
法律、法規或政策的變更可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
我們有時可能涉及法律訴訟，這可能對我們的財務狀況、營運成果、現金流以及普通股的交易價格產生重大不利影響。
與我們債務融資相關的風險
我們擁有相當程度的債務，且我們的組織章程文件對於未來可能產生的額外負債並無金額上限的限制。
較高的利率已提高我們的債務償還金額，且這樣的債務償還金額可能持續維持在較高水平。
與我們的債務相關的再融資風險。
我們的避險策略可能無法成功降低與利率相關的風險，並可能降低投資本公司之投資人整體回報。
與利益衝突相關的風險
Ashford LLC 在分拆前為 Ashford Trust 的子公司，可能能將具吸引力的投資機會導向 Ashford Trust 而非我們。
paragraphs: 本公司業務面臨許多風險，包括可能使本公司無法達成業務目標，或對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果、現金流及前景產生不利影響的風險。這些風險在下文有更詳細說明，包括但不限於以下風險：
•本公司能否籌集足夠資金及/或採取其他行動改善流動性地位，或否則符合流動性需求；
•若本公司無法償還債務本息或履行其他貸款協議項下義務，本公司貸款機構可能加速貸款餘額並對用作貸款擔保的酒店資產進行拍賣；
•資本市場的總體波動性及本公司普通股與優先股的市場價格；
•重大災害或地緣政治條件，例如俄羅斯與烏克蘭之間的衝突、以色列與巴勒斯坦與伊朗之間的衝突以及委內瑞拉持續的不穩定情況；
•資金的可取得性、條件及運用；
